title: When the Thorn Wakes
premise: Rafael Nystrom, a mercenary bound by an oath to the silent god Veth, keeps accounts for the Gilded Thorn, a guild that traffics in impossible things—bottled grief, borrowed years, names not yet spoken. When a feral child named Ilsa arrives speaking the First Tongue, Rafael realizes she carries a soul that was sold to the Hollow Court beneath Mount Ceren, and that her presence will draw the guild's enemies like wolves to blood. To save her, Rafael must break their own ledger's oldest rule, betray the guildmaster who once saved them, and descend into the court where Veth's silence began. In the end, Rafael learns the god never went silent—it was imprisoned—and by trading their own sworn soul for Ilsa's freedom, they wake the thorn: Veth's power returning through every debt ever written in the ledgers, remaking both god and mortal.
about_author: C. M. Eriksen is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing medieval debt records before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about paperwork, faith, and the people caught between them.

chapters.title: The Weight of Small Debts
chapters.summary: Rafael Nystrom audits the Gilded Thorn's ledgers, cataloguing impossible inventory while dodging guildmaster Sorrel's probing questions. POV: Rafael. Beat: weary competence masking loneliness; establishes Rafael's oath to the silent god Veth and their careful invisibility.

chapters.title: A Knock at the Waning Hour
chapters.summary: On the night of the dead moon, a child appears at the guild door, barefoot in snow, speaking a language no living throat should know. Rafael recognizes fragments from forbidden texts. POV: Rafael. Beat: unease sharpening into dread as the child's words make the ledger ink crawl.

chapters.title: The First Tongue
chapters.summary: Guild linguist Maren confirms the child—Ilsa—speaks the First Tongue, predating kingdoms and gods. Sorrel orders her hidden. Rafael dreams of a thorned crown and hears Veth's silence like ringing ears. POV: Rafael. Beat: wonder curdling into fear of what Ilsa's arrival means.

chapters.title: Ledger of Souls
chapters.summary: Searching old volumes, Rafael finds a sealed page: forty years ago, someone sold a soul to the Hollow Court beneath Mount Ceren—the payment recorded in Veth's own hand. The buyer's mark matches Ilsa's birthmark. POV: Rafael. Beat: horrified realization that the child is collateral for a divine crime.

chapters.title: Sorrel's Kindness
chapters.summary: Sorrel reveals she knows what Ilsa is and offers Rafael a choice: help smuggle the girl to the Court's brokers for a fortune, or be cast out with her. Rafael remembers Sorrel pulling them from a gutter long ago. POV: Rafael. Beat: loyalty and love weaponized against conscience.

chapters.title: The Broker's Visit
chapters.summary: A broker from beneath the mountain arrives wearing a face that doesn't quite fit, inspecting the guild and lingering near Ilsa's hiding place. Rafael lies for the first time in the guild's books. POV: Rafael. Beat: terror and exhilaration; crossing the first irreversible line.

chapters.title: What Veth Owes
chapters.summary: Rafael prays at the abandoned shrine and receives an answer—not words but a vision: Veth chained below Ceren, his voice stolen as payment. The god didn't go silent; he was silenced. POV: Rafael. Beat: shattered faith reassembling into purpose and fury.

chapters.title: Maren's Bargain
chapters.summary: Maren catches Rafael stealing maps of the mountain and instead of reporting them, demands passage on the expedition—she wants to study the First Tongue at its source. POV: Rafael. Beat: reluctant alliance; first crack in Rafael's isolation.

chapters.title: Ink and Iron
chapters.summary: Rafael falsifies the ledgers to fund the journey, erasing debts and inventing a guild mission. Each forged entry physically pains them—the oaths are woven into the writing. POV: Rafael. Beat: guilt braided with resolve; corruption begins at home.

chapters.title: Ilsa Speaks
chapters.summary: Ilsa speaks her first common words to Rafael: 'You smell like his promises.' She explains fragments—that she was born already sold, a vessel grown around a stolen soul. POV: Rafael. Beat: tenderness and horror entwined; the stakes become a child, not a concept.

chapters.title: Departure by Dark
chapters.summary: Rafael, Maren, and Ilsa slip out of the city ahead of Sorrel's hunters, guided by a debt-token that pulls toward Ceren like a compass needle. POV: Rafael. Beat: bittersweet escape; the guild that was home is now pursuit.

chapters.title: The Salt Road
chapters.summary: On the road they encounter pilgrims walking to Ceren to sell small things—memories, first loves—for survival. Rafael interviews one and records her bargain, hating how familiar the work feels. POV: Rafael. Beat: moral vertigo; seeing the trade's human cost up close.

chapters.title: Hunters in the Reeds
chapters.summary: Sorrel's enforcers ambush the party at a river crossing. Rafael kills for the first time since swearing off violence, and the act reopens old wounds and old skills. POV: Rafael. Beat: the mercenary self resurfaces, unwelcome and efficient.

chapters.title: Maren's Heresy
chapters.summary: Maren deciphers Ilsa's ramblings: the First Tongue is the language reality was drafted in, and the Hollow Court uses it to write contracts that bind even gods. POV: Maren. Beat: intellectual awe shading into terror; knowledge itself becomes dangerous.

chapters.title: The Town That Forgot
chapters.summary: They pass through a village whose inhabitants sold their memories of a single day to survive a famine—and now cannot mourn the children lost in it. Ilsa weeps for them in the First Tongue. POV: Rafael. Beat: grief without memory; the true price of the trade made flesh.

chapters.title: Sorrel's Side
chapters.summary: Interlude from Sorrel's POV: she reads Rafael's forged ledgers, understands everything, and sends word ahead to the Court anyway—because she owes the Court a debt older than Rafael. Beat: antagonist humanized; loyalty corrupted into servitude.

chapters.title: The Tollgate of Names
chapters.summary: At the mountain's threshold, a gatekeeper demands each traveler's true name as toll. Rafael pays with the name their mother gave them, feeling it peel away. POV: Rafael. Beat: sacrifice and identity loss; the descent literally costs selfhood.

chapters.title: Descent
chapters.summary: The party enters the Hollow Court's outer galleries: caverns lined with contract-stone, every wall inscribed with bargains struck across millennia. Maren reads compulsively; Ilsa hums along. POV: Rafael. Beat: claustrophobic awe; history as a prison.

chapters.title: The Face-Broker
chapters.summary: The broker from Chapter 6 reappears, offering Rafael a deal: Ilsa delivered peacefully, and Rafael's erased name restored plus a seat at Sorrel's side forever. POV: Rafael. Beat: temptation crystallized—the comfortable life offered back at the worst price.

chapters.title: Refusal
chapters.summary: Rafael refuses and fights free of the broker's gallery, but Maren is taken hostage as leverage. Ilsa, terrified, begins speaking the First Tongue involuntarily—the stolen soul stirring. POV: Rafael. Beat: failure and escalation; rescue now has a deadline.

chapters.title: The Ledger Beneath
chapters.summary: Guided by Ilsa's humming, Rafael finds the Court's master ledger—the original book from which all guild ledgers descend—and sees Veth's signature on every page. The god was the first debtor. POV: Rafael. Beat: revelation; the whole economy of souls traced to its wounded origin.

chapters.title: Audience with the Regent
chapters.summary: Rafael is granted audience with the Court's Regent, a figure assembled from surrendered faces, who explains Veth's imprisonment: the god tried to forgive all debts, and forgiveness would have unmade the Court. POV: Rafael. Beat: the antagonist's terrible logic; power justified as order.

chapters.title: Maren's Choice
chapters.summary: Offered access to the First Tongue's full grammar, Maren wavers—then burns her notes and chooses Rafael and Ilsa over knowledge. The Regent marks her for collection later. POV: Maren. Beat: loyalty chosen at personal ruin; quiet heroism.

chapters.title: The Cellar of Voices
chapters.summary: Rafael locates Veth's prison: a cellar where the god's voice is kept in jars, each containing a century of silenced speech. One jar whispers Rafael's name. POV: Rafael. Beat: heartbreak and hope; the silent god has been listening all along.

chapters.title: What the God Said
chapters.summary: Through a cracked jar, Veth speaks to Rafael: he cannot break his own contracts—but a debtor can void a debt by paying it in full, or by dying owed. He asks nothing. That's what breaks Rafael open. POV: Rafael. Beat: divine humility; the plan forms in anguish.

chapters.title: Sorrel Descends
chapters.summary: Sorrel arrives to complete her ancient debt, expecting to hand over Ilsa. Confronted by Rafael, she confesses she sold her own children's futures decades ago and has been the Court's agent ever since. POV: Sorrel. Beat: tragedy revealed; the mentor as victim-perpetrator.

chapters.title: The Offer Refused Twice
chapters.summary: Rafael offers Sorrel absolution through the ledger—recording her debt as paid by service rendered. The Court rejects the entry; only blood or souls clear accounts here. Sorrel, weeping, sides with Rafael anyway. POV: Rafael. Beat: mercy attempted and denied; alliance forged in shared damnation.

chapters.title: Ilsa Remembers
chapters.summary: The stolen soul inside Ilsa surfaces fully: she is the fragment of Veth himself, cut away as collateral when he tried to forgive the world. She remembers being whole. POV: Ilsa. Beat: devastating innocence; the child learns she was never a person, only a payment.

chapters.title: Running Out of Time
chapters.summary: The Regent moves to extract the soul early, accelerating Ilsa's dissolution. The party has one night before she unravels into contract-ink. Plans are made in whispers among the contract-walls. POV: Rafael. Beat: ticking clock; desperation sharpening into clarity.

chapters.title: The Forged Covenant
chapters.summary: Rafael commits the ultimate forgery: drafting a new covenant in the First Tongue, taught stroke by stroke by Ilsa, declaring all debts beneath Ceren void upon Veth's waking. It needs a signature of sovereign weight. POV: Rafael. Beat: audacity; the accountant turns forger of reality.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Threshold
chapters.summary: One of Sorrel's enforcers, spared in Chapter 13, sells their route to the Court. Guards seize Ilsa mid-ritual; Maren is wounded holding the corridor. POV: Rafael. Beat: betrayal's sting; everything built begins collapsing.

chapters.title: The Price of the Pen
chapters.summary: To sign the covenant, Rafael must offer something the Court values more than Ilsa's soul: their own sworn soul, the oath-bond to Veth himself. They sign. The covenant ignites. POV: Rafael. Beat: climax begins; total sacrifice offered without hesitation.

chapters.title: When the Thorn Wakes
chapters.summary: Veth wakes as the covenant takes hold: every debt ever recorded trembles, jars shatter, and the god's voice floods the caverns. The Regent unravels as its faces remember they were people. POV: multiple, converging. Beat: cathartic eruption; the silent god roars.

chapters.title: The Regent's Last Contract
chapters.summary: Dying, the Regent attempts one final contract to preserve itself, demanding Sorrel's ancient debt as anchor. Sorrel pays it willingly—with her life—freeing her children's futures. POV: Sorrel. Beat: redemption through payment; grief and grace in one stroke.

chapters.title: Aftermath in the Dark
chapters.summary: The Court collapses into ordinary stone. Rafael lies dying, soul spent, while Ilsa—now carrying the returned fragment of herself and Veth's gratitude—refuses to let the ledger record their death. POV: Ilsa. Beat: reversal; the saved becomes savior.

chapters.title: The Unwritten Entry
chapters.summary: Ilsa writes Rafael's debt as 'paid in full' in the First Tongue, and because she is part of Veth, the entry holds. Rafael breathes. Maren laughs until she cries. POV: Ilsa. Beat: miracle earned, not given; love as the final currency.

chapters.title: Homecoming
chapters.summary: The survivors return to find the Gilded Thorn transformed: with Veth awake, the guild's impossible trades are dissolving, debts forgiving themselves. Some members rage; most weep with relief. POV: Rafael. Beat: bittersweet return; the world they knew ending gently.

chapters.title: New Ledgers
chapters.summary: Rafael founds a new practice: recording not debts but gifts given freely, testing whether an economy of grace can hold. The first entry is Sorrel's name, posthumously honored. POV: Rafael. Beat: rebuilding; idealism tempered by hard-won wisdom.

chapters.title: The God Who Listens
chapters.summary: Veth, embodied faintly in Ilsa's shadow, thanks Rafael—not with power but with attention, the thing the god was denied for centuries. Rafael finally feels heard. POV: Rafael. Beat: quiet communion; belonging achieved at last.

chapters.title: When the Thorn Sleeps
chapters.summary: Years later, Rafael teaches Ilsa the accounting craft as the shrine bells ring again across the land. The last chapter closes on a new ledger's blank first page, waiting. POV: Rafael. Beat: peace earned; the story ends where all honest books begin.
